sample-1822-1: I found out a data broker was selling my location history from an app my kid put on our tablet. I never agreed to that in any way a normal person would understand. Maine should not wait for Washington to protect us — Congress has been 'about to act' on privacy my entire adult life.
sample-1822-2: I run a small pottery shop online. The compliance section for small businesses is workable — the thresholds are sensible and honestly, I don't want to collect data I don't need. It's the brokers reselling my customers' information who should be nervous, not me.
sample-1822-3: Our members support privacy in principle, but a Maine-only standard stricter than every neighboring state means Maine businesses carry compliance costs their competitors don't. We urge the committee to align with the Connecticut framework rather than creating a fifty-first standard.
sample-1822-4: I teach high school civics, and my students cannot tell you what they've consented to online — no one can. I'm neutral on this specific framework but I ask the committee: whatever passes, require consent language readable at an eighth-grade level. Otherwise none of it matters.
